project_summary: Solo creator launches an AI-powered mechanical DIY YouTube channel with a Patreon tier for paid tutorials, scripts, and CAD files. Revenue depends on YouTube ad share, Patreon subscriptions, and affiliate links. Production assumes weekly long-form videos plus a Patreon-exclusive deep-dive each month.

failure_risks.risk: Weekly long-form mechanical DIY video output is unsustainable for a solo creator who must source parts, build, film, edit, and write scripts; burnout or schedule slippage will collapse the algorithmic momentum YouTube growth depends on.

action_map.validation_step: Test whether the creator can ship 4 publishable mechanical DIY videos in 4 consecutive weeks without external help, while tracking real hours per video.
action_map.minimum_test: Run a 4-week production sprint: produce and publish 4 videos using only the tools, parts budget, and time the creator currently has. Log every hour spent on sourcing, building, filming, editing, thumbnails, and writing.
action_map.success_metric: All 4 videos shipped on schedule with average production time at or below 25 hours per video and creator self-rated burnout risk under 6/10.
action_map.failure_threshold: Any missed publish date, average production time above 35 hours per video, or burnout score 8/10+ at the end of week 4.
action_map.next_action: If success: lock in weekly cadence and begin building 2-week content buffer. If failure: drop to biweekly cadence, narrow video scope, or hire an editor before launch.

failure_risks.risk: The 'AI-powered' angle is undifferentiated and may not translate to Patreon willingness-to-pay; mechanical DIY audiences tend to value craftsmanship and authenticity, not AI-generated scripts or designs, so the paid tier may attract subscribers at a rate too low to sustain the project.

action_map.validation_step: Test whether the target audience will actually pay for AI-augmented mechanical DIY content vs. treating AI as a turnoff.
action_map.minimum_test: Before launching the channel, post 3 sample videos and a Patreon landing page describing the paid tier explicitly (AI-assisted CAD files, AI-generated build variations, prompt walkthroughs). Drive 1,000 targeted clicks via Reddit, niche forums, and paid ads.
action_map.success_metric: At least 2% landing-page-to-email conversion AND 0.5% landing-page-to-paid conversion within 30 days of the test.
action_map.failure_threshold: Conversion below 1% to email or zero paid signups after 1,000 clicks; OR qualitative comments dominated by AI skepticism.
action_map.next_action: If success: proceed with AI angle as a primary differentiator. If failure: pivot positioning so AI is a behind-the-scenes tool rather than the brand, and reframe the Patreon tier around build files, member Q&A, and early access.

failure_risks.risk: Revenue model concentrates on two platforms (YouTube and Patreon) whose policies on AI-generated content, monetization, and adult/dangerous mechanical builds are tightening; a single demonetization event or policy change can cut income to near-zero with no recourse.

action_map.validation_step: Confirm that the planned content format complies with current YouTube and Patreon policies on AI disclosure, monetization eligibility, and dangerous activity guidelines, AND that the creator has a viable off-platform fallback channel.
action_map.minimum_test: Submit the first 3 finished videos through YouTube's monetization review and apply for a Patreon creator account with full disclosure of the AI-augmented format. In parallel, set up an email list and a self-hosted store as a backup distribution path.
action_map.success_metric: Both platforms approve the content for monetization without restrictions, AND the email list captures at least 200 subscribers in the first 60 days.
action_map.failure_threshold: Either platform restricts monetization, demands format changes that conflict with the value proposition, or the email list grows below 50 subscribers in 60 days.
action_map.next_action: If success: maintain the email list as a permanent off-platform asset and continue. If failure: rebuild the model around direct sales, Skool/Discord community, or a paid newsletter before scaling.
